subject: general
question: ________ is a sulphur containing amino acid.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cysteine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cysteine** is an amino acid that contains sulfur in its structure.
 
• It is one of the non-essential amino acids, which means the body can synthesize it.
 
• Cysteine plays a crucial role in the biosynthesis of proteins, glutathione, and coenzyme A.
 
• It is important for the stability of protein structures due to the formation of disulfide bonds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amino Acids**

 
 
• Amino acids are organic compounds that combine to form proteins, which are the building blocks of life.
 
• There are 20 standard amino acids, which can be categorized into essential and non-essential amino acids.
 
• Essential amino acids cannot be made by the body and must be obtained from the diet.
 
• Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the body.
 
 
 
• **Sulfur-Containing Amino Acids**
 
 
• Two of the 20 standard amino acids contain sulfur: cysteine and methionine.
 
• Sulfur-containing amino acids are important for various metabolic processes and the synthesis of important biomolecules.
 
• They are also crucial for the structure and function of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Cysteine**
 
 
• Cysteine is involved in the detoxification processes in the liver.
 
• It is a precursor to the antioxidant glutathione, which helps protect cells from oxidative damage.
 
• Cysteine is also involved in the formation of disulfide bonds, which help stabilize the three-dimensional structure of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Disulfide Bonds**
 
 
• Disulfide bonds are covalent bonds that form between the sulfur atoms of two cysteine residues within or between protein molecules.
 
• They play a critical role in maintaining the stability and functionality of proteins.
 
• The formation of disulfide bonds is a post-translational modification that occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum.
